title: Gammeldags Æblekage
subtitle: Old-Fashioned Danish Apple Cake
description: A classic Danish coffee-table dessert made from apple compote and homemade buttered breadcrumb "rasp," layered with whipped cream. A great way to use up stale bread, with a creamy, comforting texture — just like grandma used to make.

sections.name: Breadcrumb Rasp
ingredients: 4 slices day-old bread (white bread, pita, or toast bread)
1¾ oz (50 g) of the dried breadcrumbs, from above
steps: Pulse the bread in a blender or food processor until finely crumbed (leave a bit coarser if you prefer more texture).
Spread the crumbs on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Dry in the oven for about 25–30 minutes, turning once or twice, until crisp. Let cool.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the dried crumbs and sugar, and toast gently, stirring, until golden and crisp. Set aside.

sections.name: Apple Compote
ingredients: 10½ oz (300 g) apples, peeled and cored (about 2 medium apples)
¼ cup + 1 tbsp (½ dl / 50 ml) water
steps: Cut the apples into wedges, remove the core, then chop into rough cubes. Simmer in a pot with the water, sugar, lemon juice, and vanilla powder until soft.
Cover and let the compote simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Let cool once soft.

sections.name: Whipped Cream & Assembly
ingredients: ¾ cup + 2 tbsp (2 dl / 200 ml) heavy whipping cream
steps: Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Get out a few serving glasses. Layer apple compote, then buttered breadcrumb rasp, then a few crushed macaroons (optional). Repeat the layers.
Finish with whipped cream on top, just like a classic old-fashioned æblekage.

tip: It's the butter and sugar that turn plain toasted breadcrumbs into proper "æblekage rasp." If you just dry the crumbs without them, you get an ordinary rasp for savory cooking instead — a good way to use up stale bread and keep it longer in a bag or airtight container.
